title: Femtosecond laser combined with non-chopping rotation phacoemulsification technique for soft-nucleus cataract surgery: a prospective study

indication: Soft-nucleus cataract (Pentacam nucleus staging grade 1-3); preoperative ECD below 1500 cells/mm2, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, uveitis, AMD and previous intraocular surgery or trauma excluded; subgroups by nucleus grade

groups.indication: Soft-nucleus cataract, Pentacam nucleus staging grade 1
groups.description: Femtosecond laser pretreatment (LenSx, cylindrical lens-softening pattern, laser capsulotomy and incisions) combined with the non-chopping rotation phacoemulsification technique (subgroup 1, the study group; patients who elected laser surgery); Pentacam nucleus staging grade 1 subgroup

groups.indication: Soft-nucleus cataract, Pentacam nucleus staging grade 1
groups.description: Conventional manual cataract surgery (2.8 mm clear corneal incision, manual capsulorhexis) with the non-chopping rotation technique (subgroup 2; randomized among manual patients); Pentacam nucleus staging grade 1 subgroup

exclusions.what: Table 1 CCT, CDVA and aqueous flare rows
Pooled technique groups (22 eyes each) across nucleus grades
exclusions.reason: ECD and ECL are tabulated only per technique and nucleus grade; no pooled values exist

notes: Femtosecond pretreatment combined with non-chopping rotation is the technique the authors introduce (the study group): treated. The two conventional manual techniques are control groups. Nucleus grade subgroups are baseline-condition subgroups.

Allocation: patients chose laser surgery; the remaining patients were randomized between the two manual techniques; the laser group was paired 1:1 with manual cases by age, sex and nucleus stage (Methods).
Values are percent loss from each column's own preoperative ECD (value_kind percent_loss with reference_cell); the table gives no postoperative absolute ECD.
Group n_reported and series n are omitted because the per-grade subgroup sizes appear only in Figure 4 (an image).
